title: 38 mm rated bag hook proof
what_it_proves: bought hook meets the >= 2200 N purchase rating
steps: hook on the 5 mm steel pin; 38 mm webbing loop on the hook bed; pull with the come-along to 2120 N on the crane scale; hold 60 s; release; check the gate closes
pass_fail: 5 of 5 hold 2120 N for 60 s and the gate closes after
notes: production: 1 hook per lot of 25 to 1415 N

title: meat-strap hook proof (R-29)
what_it_proves: assumed 1500 N meat-strap hook rating
safety_at_stake: meat hook SF 2.48 on 605 N leg

pass_fail: 5 of 5 hold 910 N for 1 min, gate closes
notes: CONFLICT: BUILD_PLAN says 910 N, meat_haul_modes says 830 N; 910 N (= 1.5 x 605 N) used. Retired if S-01 (one rated hook for all 12) is adopted

title: cam buckle slip on 38 mm webbing (R-29)

gates: IM cams and the under-strap cam

steps: thread the cam as in the pack; paint-pen mark on the webbing at the cam mouth; pull to 910 N; hold 1 min; measure the mark
pass_fail: slip < 3 mm at 910 N for 1 min, 5 of 5
notes: same 910 N vs 830 N conflict as MT-2

title: hipbelt heavy ladder-lock slip, corrected 2:1 routing
what_it_proves: record slip load 490 N (0.5 x rating, ASSUMPTION)

specimen: 5 heavy 25 mm ladder locks on 25 mm webbing, routed anchor -> D-ring -> lock
steps: mark webbing; pull the lock leg to 426 N, hold 1 min; then pull on until it slips and record the load
pass_fail: no slip at 426 N (1.5 x 284 N); slip load >= 490 N keeps the record
notes: pass number derived here: 1.5 x 284 N = 426 N (doc gives only 'as the record notes')

title: guy ladder lock + tri-glide keeper slip

pass_fail: slip < 5 mm over 10 cycles

pass_fail: 5 of 5 hold 910 N for 1 min, no broken stitch

pass_fail: 5 of 5 hold 2120 N, no stitch break, no laminate tear

title: wash-swatch fray, seams without binding

pass_fail: no fray past the second row on any swatch
notes: B-1 is already in B.2: a fail adds 36.4 g back. R-12 / S-03 gate is the same test (merged)

title: belt face friction
what_it_proves: belt face friction mu against base layers
specimen: belt face fabric with and without the grip print; polyester and merino base layers, dry and sweaty
steps: base layer taped to a board; 500 g weighted sled with the face fabric on it; raise one end slowly until it slides; read the angle in phyphox; mu = tan(angle); 5 runs each
pass_fail: mu >= 0.45 credits the grip print
notes: ASSUMPTION: tilt-board static mu replaces the ASTM D1894-style sled pull (no low-range force gauge in the kits); grip print adds 4.9 g if adopted

title: PAHT-CF fatigue coupons, 0.30 then 0.40

pass_fail: 3/3 run-outs to 1e5, stiffness loss <= 10 %, no crack; static XY >= 79.2 MPa, Z >= 42.3 MPa
notes: grams = midpoint of -50..-70 g (frame_h1.md §6), only if 0.40 passes. Machine: 8 runs x 27.8 h. CT-B1 merged here
